result:
REST: one URL per resource, HTTP verbs, status codes. Wins on simplicity, HTTP caching (CDNs, ETags, browser cache work out of the box), mature tooling, easy rate limiting and monitoring per endpoint, low learning curve. Costs: over/under-fetching → multiple round trips or bloated payloads, endpoint sprawl as client needs diverge, versioning headaches (`/v2/...`).

GraphQL: single endpoint, typed schema, client picks fields. Wins on flexible queries (one request fetches nested data), strong typing → codegen and introspection, schema evolution without versions (deprecate fields), good fit for many heterogeneous clients (web, mobile). Costs: HTTP caching mostly lost (POSTs to one URL) → need client-side caches (Apollo, Relay) or persisted queries; N+1 resolver problem → DataLoader-style batching required; arbitrary queries → need depth/complexity limits against abusive queries; per-field authorization is more work; errors return 200 with `errors` array, muddying monitoring; file uploads and streaming are awkward; heavier server and client tooling.

Verdict: default to REST for public APIs, simple CRUD, cache-heavy or resource-oriented services, small teams. Pick GraphQL when multiple clients need different shapes of deeply related data and you control those clients, and you're willing to invest in query cost limits, batching, and client caching.
